R062-01.notes: Passage explains the mechanism (setae, van der Waals, peel release) and the elimination/testing process. A: last paragraph says synthetics do NOT yet match geckos; no prediction. C: no evolutionary history. D: glue/suction/hooks are only dismissed in P1, not compared for strength.

R062-02.notes: P1: 'Glue was ruled out because gecko feet have no glands that secrete anything sticky.' A is the reason given against suction; B against hooks; C is the P3 water-film test.

R062-03.notes: P3: 'If water films were essential, the setae should have gripped the water-attracting surfaces far more strongly.' A is what the actual (similar-grip) result supported. B: humidity was later found to help, and the test was not about humidity having no effect. D: rough vs smooth not tested.

R062-04.notes: The clause concedes humidity strengthens grip 'somewhat' while vdW remains 'the main source' -- a qualification. B: 'somewhat' does not disprove anything. C: no claim about geckos avoiding dry places. D: release is introduced in P4, not by this clause.

R062-05.notes: 'Any single contact is feeble, but billions of them together produce a grip strong' -- contrast with strong gives weak. A and C are senses for people/animals; B fits arguments, not physical contacts.

R062-06.notes: Tape 'comes off more easily when pulled from one edge'; setae 'peel away... a few at a time.' 'Far less force' slightly intensifies 'more easily' but is consistent with 'almost absent in another' direction. A contradicts P1 (no sticky secretion). C: passage says geckos keep working after thousands of steps. D: no strip arrangement described.

R062-07.notes: vdW forces act only when branches come 'extremely close' to the surface, so a surface they cannot approach closely would weaken grip. B: grip was similar on water-repelling surfaces. C: geckos hold polished glass. D: geckos still clung in a vacuum.

flags.note: Cross-item cue: R062-03's choice C ('thin films of water were the main source of the gecko's adhesion') and its stem effectively supply this answer. Minor, since the item is direct recall anyway.

R062-08.notes: P3: 'Some researchers suspected that thin films of water... were doing the work through capillary attraction.' A and B are the P1 'obvious guesses' that were ruled out before the setae/vdW account, not alternatives raised against it; D (electric charges) is never mentioned.

R062-09.notes: Synthetics 'can now hold heavy objects... and release them cleanly, though none yet matches the gecko's ability to stay clean and keep working.' A contradicts 'hold heavy objects'; B contradicts 'none yet matches'; C: they are explicitly copies of gecko feet.

R062-10.notes: P4: 'When a gecko curls its toes upward, the setae peel away from the surface a few at a time.' B: no secretions (P1). C: release is active, via angle. D: pulling straight out is the hard way, per the tape analogy.
